en: haphazard way of doing things; rough guesswork

examples.ko: 예산을 주먹구구로 짜면 나중에 문제가 생겨요.
examples.en: If you make the budget by rough guesswork, problems will arise later.
This plan is too sloppy.
It's a rough calculation, so it isn't exact.
Don't rely on guesswork; check the numbers.

examples.ko: 주먹구구가 아니라 근거 있는 자료가 필요해요.
examples.en: We need data with evidence, not guesswork.
A rough guess is fine, so please tell me roughly.

explain: 정확하게 따지지 않고 대충 어림으로 계산하거나 일하는 것을 말해요. 보통 안 좋은 뜻으로 쓰고, '대충'보다 일 처리 방식을 비판하는 느낌이 있어요. '주먹구구로 하다, 주먹구구가 되다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: A haphazard plan soon runs into trouble.
phrases.nuance_ko: '주먹구구'와 같은 뜻으로, 일하는 방식이 대충이라고 할 때 흔히 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '주먹구구'; commonly used to describe a sloppy way of working.

phrases.en: If you calculate money roughly, it's easy to be wrong.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정확히 따지지 않고 어림으로 계산한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means calculating by rough guess rather than precisely.

phrases.en: You shouldn't do the work carelessly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일을 대충 한다고 비판할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to criticize doing work sloppily.

explain_en: It means calculating or working roughly without checking things properly. It is usually negative and criticizes the way work is done more than '대충' does. It is used as '주먹구구로 하다' or '주먹구구가 되다'.

examples.en: The diameter of this circle is 10 centimeters.
I bought a pipe with a large diameter.
I measured the ball's diameter with a ruler.

examples.ko: 나사 직경이 맞지 않아서 안 들어가요.
examples.en: The screw diameter doesn't match, so it won't fit.
The pizza is 30 cm across, so it's enough for two.

examples.ko: 직경을 알면 원의 둘레도 구할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you know the diameter, you can also find the circle's circumference.

explain: 원이나 공의 가운데를 지나는 가장 긴 선의 길이예요. 같은 뜻으로 '지름'을 더 많이 쓰고, '직경'은 수학·공학 글에서 보여요. '반지름'은 직경의 반이에요.

phrases.en: I measure the diameter of the circle with a ruler.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻이고 일상에서 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, and more common in daily life.

phrases.en: Try measuring the ball's diameter with a ruler.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길이를 잴 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for measuring length.

phrases.example: 이 나무는 직경이 커서 한 사람이 안을 수 없어요.
phrases.en: This tree has a large diameter, so one person can't hug it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크기를 말할 때 형용사와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with adjectives to describe size.

explain_en: It is the length of the longest line through the center of a circle or sphere. 지름 is the more common word for the same thing, while 직경 appears in math and engineering. 반지름 is half of it.

en: to be unusually precious; to be rare

examples.ko: 박물관에는 세상에 하나뿐인 진귀한 보석이 있어요.
examples.en: The museum has a rare, precious jewel that is the only one in the world.

examples.ko: 시장에서 진귀한 과일을 발견해서 하나 사 봤어요.
examples.en: I found a rare fruit at the market and bought one.

examples.ko: 그 책은 구하기 어려울 만큼 진귀해요.
examples.en: That book is so rare that it's hard to get.

examples.ko: 할머니 집에는 진귀해 보이는 도자기가 많아요.
examples.en: There is a lot of valuable-looking pottery at my grandmother's house.

examples.ko: 이렇게 진귀한 음식은 처음 먹어 봐요.
examples.en: This is the first time I've eaten such an unusual delicacy.

examples.ko: 진귀하다고 해서 모두 비싼 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Just because something is rare doesn't mean it's all expensive.

explain: '귀하다'와 비슷하지만 흔하지 않고 신기하다는 느낌이 더 있어요. '진귀한 보석', '진귀한 물건'처럼 물건 앞에서 많이 써요. 대화에서는 '귀하다'나 '희귀하다'를 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.example: 그 식당에서는 진귀한 음식을 맛볼 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can taste rare and special food at that restaurant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 흔하지 않아서 특별한 음식 앞에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put before food that is special because it isn't common.

phrases.en: This ceramic piece looks very rare and precious.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습을 보고 드물고 귀한 물건처럼 느껴질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something looks rare and valuable at first sight.

phrases.example: 사람들은 그 보석을 아주 진귀하게 여겨요.
phrases.en: People regard that jewel as very rare and precious.
phrases.nuance_ko: 흔하지 않아서 귀하다고 생각한다는 뜻으로, 부사 꼴로 활용해 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to regard something as precious because it is uncommon; uses the adverb form.
phrases.en_equiv: to regard as rare and precious

explain_en: It is similar to '귀하다' but adds a sense of being uncommon and remarkable. It is often used before objects, as in '진귀한 보석' or '진귀한 물건'. In conversation people may also say '귀하다' or '희귀하다'.

t90.ax: That book is so rare that it's hard to get.

en: to be rare; to be scarce

examples.en: This coin is rare because there are few of them.
Scarce resources tend to go up in price.
Jobs like this have become rare these days.

examples.ko: 그 책은 희소하다는 이유로 비싸게 팔려요.
examples.en: That book sells for a high price because it's rare.
It's a bird that is rarely found, so it is being protected.

examples.ko: 이 약은 원료가 희소해서 가격이 비싸요.
examples.en: The raw material for this medicine is scarce, so the price is high.

explain: 수가 적어서 귀하다는 느낌이고, 값이나 가치와 연결되는 경우가 많아요. 일상에서는 '드물다', '귀하다'라고 말하고, '희소가치'라는 말도 자주 써요. '희소식'은 기쁜 소식이라는 뜻의 완전히 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: This card is expensive because its rarity value is high.
phrases.nuance_ko: 드물어서 생기는 가치를 말하는 합친 말로, 값이 비싼 이유를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A compound meaning value that comes from rarity, used to explain a high price.

phrases.en: This item is getting scarcer every year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 점점 수가 줄어드는 변화를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes something gradually becoming rarer.

phrases.en: A chance this good is rare.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '희소하다'보다 '드물다'를 더 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In everyday talk, 드물다 is used more often than 희소하다.

explain_en: Formal/written; very few in number or amount (희소한 동전) It means rare because of small numbers, often linked to price or value. In daily speech people say '드물다' or '귀하다', and the term '희소가치' is also common. '희소식' means good news and is a completely different word.

t90.ax: Scarce resources tend to go up in price.

examples.ko: 저는 서울 본토박이라서 길을 잘 알아요.
examples.en: I'm a native Seoulite, so I know the streets well.
I heard the owner of this restaurant is a Busan native.
A local-born person's way of speaking is hard to learn from books.

examples.ko: 제주 본토박이 할머니가 길을 알려 주셨어요.
examples.en: An old lady who was born and raised in Jeju showed me the way.

examples.ko: 본토박이한테 맛집을 물어보는 게 제일 좋아요.
examples.en: Asking a local-born person about good restaurants is best.
That person speaks the dialect like a native.

explain: 그 지역에서 태어나 오래 산 사람을 말해요. '토박이'만 쓰기도 하고, 그냥 그곳에 사는 사람은 '현지인'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 저는 서울 본토박이는 아니지만 서울이 고향 같아요.
phrases.en: I'm not a Seoul native, but Seoul feels like my hometown.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지역 이름 뒤에 붙여 그곳 출신으로 오래 산 사람을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put after a place name to mean a long-time local person from there.

phrases.en: That grandmother is a native of this neighborhood.
phrases.nuance_ko: '본토박이'를 줄여 말한 것이고 일상에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of '본토박이' that is used more often in daily talk.

phrases.example: 본토박이 주민들이 마을 역사를 가장 잘 알아요.
phrases.en: The native residents know the village's history best.
phrases.nuance_ko: '주민' 앞에 붙여 그 지역에서 오래 산 사람들을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before '주민' it refers to people who have lived there a long time.

explain_en: Person born and raised in a place; refers to people. It refers to someone who was born in a place and has lived there a long time. People also just say '토박이', and someone who simply lives there is a '현지인'.

en: influential person; powerful person; power broker

examples.ko: 그 모임에서는 회장이 가장 큰 실력자예요.
examples.en: In that group, the chairperson is the most powerful figure.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 정치계의 숨은 실력자로 알려져 있어요.
examples.en: He is known as a hidden power broker in the political world.
A rumor spread that an influential person helped from behind the scenes.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 실력자라고 불리는 분이 이장님이에요.
examples.en: The person called the powerful figure of our neighborhood is the village head.
He is an influential person in town, but he is always humble.

examples.ko: 실력자에게 잘 보이려고 애쓰는 사람들이 많아요.
examples.en: There are many people who try hard to impress influential people.

explain: 높은 직함이 없어도 실제로 힘이 큰 사람을 말할 때 어울려요. '실세'와 비슷하고, '숨은 실력자'라는 말을 자주 써요. 보통 조직이나 모임, 정치 이야기에서 나와요.

phrases.en: I hear that person is the real power in this group.
phrases.nuance_ko: '실력자'와 비슷하고, 실제 힘을 가진 사람을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 실력자, pointing to the person who holds real power.

phrases.en: He is a very powerful figure in the company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘이 아주 크다는 것을 더해 말하는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing that stresses how great the person's power is.

phrases.en: He is regarded as an influential figure in the industry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들이 그렇게 인정한다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means people widely recognize him as such.

explain_en: Person holding real power in a group — influence from actual ability or position. It fits a person who holds real power even without a high title. It is similar to '실세', and '숨은 실력자' (hidden power broker) is a common phrase. It usually comes up when talking about organizations, groups or politics.

t90.ax: In that group, the chairperson is the most powerful figure.

en: to be mean; to be underhand; to be base

examples.ko: 약속을 어기고 몰래 도망가다니 정말 야비해요.
examples.en: Breaking your promise and sneaking away is really low.

examples.ko: 약한 사람을 이용하는 건 야비한 행동이에요.
examples.en: Taking advantage of weak people is a despicable act.
He lied with a sly, nasty smile.
I felt that the person who talks behind people's backs was mean.

examples.ko: 겉으로는 친절한데 속은 야비해서 믿을 수 없어요.
examples.en: He seems kind outside, but he's mean inside, so I can't trust him.

examples.ko: 경기 중에 상대를 속인 건 야비했어요.
examples.en: Tricking the opponent during the match was underhanded.

explain: 행동이 비겁하고 정정당당하지 못할 때 쓰는 강한 말이에요. 구어체로 가볍게 말할 때는 '치사하다'를 많이 쓰고, 야비하다는 더 무겁게 비판하는 느낌이에요. 사람이나 행동, 웃음, 수법 등에 붙여 말해요.

phrases.example: 거짓말로 친구를 속이는 건 야비한 행동이에요.
phrases.en: Deceiving a friend with lies is a mean act.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비겁하고 정정당당하지 않은 행동을 비판할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to criticize cowardly and unfair behavior.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 야비하게 웃으면서 돈을 받았어요.
phrases.en: He took the money with a sly, mean smile.
phrases.nuance_ko: 웃는 모습에서 비겁하고 나쁜 속마음이 보일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a smile reveals a base and cowardly intent.
phrases.en_equiv: to smile in a mean way

phrases.en: I'm not that mean.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자신은 비겁한 사람이 아니라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you are not a base or cowardly person.

explain_en: It is a strong word for behavior that is cowardly and not fair. In casual speech people often say '치사하다' for a lighter feeling, while 야비하다 criticizes more heavily. You can use it for a person, an action, a smile or a method.

t90.ax: He lied with a sly, nasty smile.

en: to be intimate; to be friendly; to be close

examples.en: The two sisters get along really well.
I read the story of the loving brothers.
My parents always live in harmony.
They are neighbors known as a loving couple.
The brothers are close, which is nice to see.
The classmates cleaned up together in a friendly way.

explain: 주로 '의좋게 지내다', '의좋은 형제/부부'처럼 써요. 형제, 부부, 친구처럼 가까운 사이에 어울리고, 일상 대화에서는 '사이가 좋다'가 더 흔해요. '의가 좋다'라고도 해요.

phrases.example: 두 형제는 어릴 때부터 의좋게 지냈어요.
phrases.en: The two brothers have gotten along well since they were young.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의좋게'는 부사형이에요. 사이가 좋게 함께 지내는 모습을 말할 때 가장 흔히 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form 의좋게; the most common way to say people live or get along closely.

phrases.example: 의좋은 부부를 보면 저도 기분이 좋아져요.
phrases.en: Seeing a loving married couple makes me feel good too.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의좋은'은 명사를 꾸미는 관형형이에요. 형제, 부부, 친구처럼 가까운 사이에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form 의좋은; fits close pairs such as siblings, couples, or friends.

phrases.en: Those brothers are famous for getting along well.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의좋다'를 풀어 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An expanded way of saying 의좋다.

explain_en: It is mostly used in forms like '의좋게 지내다' and '의좋은 형제/부부'. It suits close relationships such as siblings, couples and friends, while '사이가 좋다' is more common in daily talk. It can also be said '의가 좋다'.

examples.en: The children grew up and all became independent.
The grown-up son works alongside his father.
My parents raised me until I grew up.

examples.ko: 막내는 어릴 때는 약했지만 장성하고 나서는 건강해졌어요.
examples.en: The youngest child was weak when little but became healthy once grown up.

examples.ko: 아이가 장성하는 동안 할머니가 늘 곁에 계셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother was always by the child's side while the child grew up.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 장성하여 훌륭한 의사가 되었어요.
examples.en: The child grew up and became a fine doctor.

explain: '크다'나 '자라다'와 비슷하지만, '장성하다'는 어른이 될 만큼 다 컸다는 느낌이라 어린아이에게는 쓰지 않아요. 보통 '장성한 자녀'처럼 부모 입장에서 말해요.

phrases.en: The grown children give their parents spending money.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부모 입장에서 다 큰 아이들을 말할 때 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase, from a parent's point of view.

phrases.en: My son grew up and got married.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다 큰 뒤에 일어난 일을 이어서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Links what happened after someone grew up.

phrases.en: The child has grown up and become a college student.
phrases.nuance_ko: '장성하다'보다 쉽고 일상에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler, everyday way to say it.

explain_en: It is close to '크다' and '자라다', but '장성하다' implies someone has grown enough to be an adult, so it is not used for young children. It is usually said from a parent's view, as in '장성한 자녀' (grown-up children).

en: to praise; to extol; to laud

examples.en: People praised that doctor's sacrifice.

examples.ko: 역사책은 그 왕을 훌륭한 지도자로 칭송해요.
examples.en: History books praise that king as a great leader.
Fans are praising the player's effort.
His courage deserves everyone's praise.

examples.ko: 그의 선행을 칭송하는 글이 신문에 실렸어요.
examples.en: An article praising his good deeds ran in the newspaper.
Nobody praised that work.

explain: '칭찬하다'보다 격식 있고 무게가 있어서 업적이나 덕 같은 큰 것에 어울려요. 일상 대화에서 친구나 가족을 칭찬할 때는 '칭찬하다'를 쓰는 게 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The citizens praised the firefighter with one voice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 사람이 함께 한목소리로 칭송한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means many people praise someone together in one voice.

phrases.en: The newspaper hailed him as a hero.
phrases.nuance_ko: 'N을 …(으)로 칭송하다' 형태로 어떻게 높이 평가하는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In the 'N을 …(으)로 칭송하다' pattern, it says how someone is highly regarded.

phrases.en: The teacher praised my presentation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 가족이나 친구에게 쓰기에는 이 말이 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural for everyday use with family or friends.

explain_en: Public admiration of someone's merits, written tone. It is more formal and weighty than '칭찬하다', fitting big things like achievements or virtue. When praising a friend or family member in daily talk, '칭찬하다' sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 저는 경제관념이 없어서 돈이 금방 없어져요.
examples.en: I have no sense of economy, so my money disappears quickly.
We teach our child a sense of money management from a young age.
A sense of economy starts with managing your allowance.
I asked a friend who is good with money for advice.
He lacks a sense of economy and has no plan either.
I heard the school gives lessons on money sense.

explain: '경제관념이 있다/없다/투철하다/부족하다'처럼 써요. 무조건 아끼는 '절약'과 달리 돈의 가치를 알고 계획적으로 쓰는 마음을 말해요. 돈을 헤프게 쓰는 사람에게 '경제관념이 없다'고 말해요.

phrases.example: 제 친구는 경제관념이 투철해서 낭비하지 않아요.
phrases.en: My friend has a strong sense of money and never wastes it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 계획적으로 쓰는 마음이 아주 강하다고 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A compliment for someone who is very careful and planned with money.
phrases.en_equiv: to have a firm sense of economy

phrases.example: 동생은 경제관념이 부족해서 용돈을 금방 써요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling lacks a sense of money and spends allowance quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '없다'보다 조금 부드럽게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A softer way to say 없다.
phrases.en_equiv: to lack a sense of economy

phrases.en: People with a sense of money keep a household account book.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈의 가치를 알고 잘 쓰는 사람을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes someone who knows the value of money and uses it well.
phrases.en_equiv: to have a sense of economy

explain_en: It is used as '경제관념이 있다/없다/투철하다/부족하다'. Unlike '절약', which is simply saving, it means knowing the value of money and spending with a plan. For someone who spends carelessly, people say '경제관념이 없다'.

examples.ko: 고액권을 잔돈으로 바꿔 주실 수 있어요?
examples.en: Could you change this large bill into small change?

examples.ko: 지갑에 고액권만 있어서 버스를 못 탔어요.
examples.en: I only had large bills in my wallet, so I couldn't take the bus.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 고액권을 받지 않는다고 해요.
examples.en: I heard this shop does not accept large bills.

examples.ko: 고액권 지폐에는 위조를 막는 기능이 더 많아요.
examples.en: Large-denomination notes have more anti-counterfeiting features.
I exchanged large bills for small ones at the bank.

examples.ko: 고액권이 나오고 나서 현금 쓰기가 편해졌어요.
examples.en: Using cash became more convenient after the large bills came out.

explain: 반대말은 '소액권'이에요. 가게에서 '큰돈'이나 '큰 지폐'라고도 말하고, '고액권을 잔돈으로 바꾸다'가 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.

phrases.en: You need small bills to ride the bus.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고액권'의 반대말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 고액권.

phrases.en: I changed a large bill into 1,000-won notes at a shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰돈을 잔돈으로 바꿀 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common when breaking a large bill into change.

phrases.en: I only have large bills. Is that okay?
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '고액권' 대신 쉽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday way to say 고액권.

explain_en: The opposite is '소액권' (small-denomination bill). In shops people also say '큰돈' or '큰 지폐', and '고액권을 잔돈으로 바꾸다' is a very common phrase.

examples.en: The government announced an austerity policy this year.
The company got into trouble, so it switched to a tight budget.
Because of the belt-tightening, salaries didn't go up.
Our household is in austerity mode these days too.
When the economy gets worse, every country goes into austerity.
If austerity drags on, people's spending falls.

explain: 뉴스에서는 '긴축 정책', '긴축 재정'처럼 나라나 회사가 돈 쓰는 것을 줄일 때 써요. 가정에서는 '긴축 모드'처럼 농담 섞어 말하기도 해요. 반대 방향의 말은 '확장'이에요.

phrases.example: 회사는 매출이 줄어서 긴축 경영에 들어갔어요.
phrases.en: The company went into austerity management because sales dropped.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사가 비용을 줄이며 운영한다는 뜻으로 경제 뉴스에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means a company runs while cutting costs; common in business news.

phrases.example: 정부가 물가를 잡으려고 긴축 정책을 폈어요.
phrases.en: The government adopted an austerity policy to control prices.
phrases.nuance_ko: '긴축 정책'을 '펴다'와 함께 쓰면 나라가 실제로 정책을 시행한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paired with 펴다, it means a government actually carries out the policy.

phrases.example: 월급날 전이라 이번 주는 긴축 모드예요.
phrases.en: It's before payday, so this week I'm in austerity mode.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 돈을 아끼는 시기를 농담처럼 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A playful everyday way to say you are cutting spending for a while.

explain_en: In the news it appears as '긴축 정책' or '긴축 재정' when a country or company cuts spending. At home people sometimes say '긴축 모드' jokingly. The opposite direction is '확장' (expansion).

examples.en: How much is the tax I have to pay this year?
The tax amount differs depending on income.
The tax amount is written separately on the receipt.
If you get deductions, the tax amount goes down.

examples.ko: 세액을 계산해 주는 프로그램을 써 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried a program that calculates the tax amount.

examples.ko: 신고서에 세액을 잘못 적어서 다시 냈어요.
examples.en: I wrote the wrong tax amount on the return, so I filed it again.

explain: '세금'은 세금 전체를 말하고, '세액'은 실제로 내야 하는 금액 숫자를 가리켜서 계산서, 신고서, 영수증에서 많이 보여요. '세액 공제'처럼 세금 용어와 함께 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I received a tax credit in the year-end tax settlement.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내야 할 세금 금액에서 직접 빼 주는 것을 말하는 세금 용어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A tax term for an amount subtracted directly from the tax you owe.

phrases.en: I calculated the tax amount and wrote it on the return.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세금을 얼마 내야 하는지 숫자로 구할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when working out in numbers how much tax is due.

phrases.example: 납부 세액은 고지서에서 확인할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can check the tax amount to pay on the bill.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 내야 하는 세금 금액을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the tax amount you actually have to pay.

explain_en: The actual amount of tax owed or paid. '세금' is tax in general, while '세액' is the actual number you have to pay, so you see it on invoices, tax returns and receipts. It often appears in tax terms such as '세액 공제' (tax credit).

en: to turn a profit; to make a good deal

examples.ko: 이번 달은 보너스까지 받아서 정말 수지맞았어요.
examples.en: I got a bonus this month too, so I really came out ahead.

examples.ko: 싸게 산 가방이 알고 보니 명품이라니, 수지맞았네요.
examples.en: The bag I bought cheap turned out to be a luxury brand. What a bargain!

examples.ko: 친구 덕분에 공짜로 여행을 다녀와서 수지맞은 기분이에요.
examples.en: I got to go on a trip for free thanks to my friend, so I feel like I came out ahead.

examples.ko: 이 가격에 밥까지 주다니 수지맞는 장사네요.
examples.en: Meals included at this price? That's a profitable deal.

examples.ko: 쿠폰을 쓰면 훨씬 더 수지맞을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you use a coupon, you can come out much further ahead.

examples.ko: 오늘 장사가 잘돼서 수지맞았다고 사장님이 웃으셨어요.
examples.en: The owner smiled and said business was good today and they had made a nice profit.

explain: 주로 '수지맞았어요', '수지맞는 장사'처럼 이익을 봤을 때 가볍게 말해요. 비슷한 말로 '이득을 보다'가 있고, '횡재하다'는 뜻밖의 큰 이익을 얻었을 때 써요.

phrases.example: 이 가게는 수지맞는 장사를 하고 있어요.
phrases.en: This shop is doing profitable business.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이익이 많이 남는 장사를 가볍게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual way to describe a business that earns a good profit.

phrases.en: You even got a free gift, so you came out ahead!
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람이 이익을 본 것을 부러워하거나 축하할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to congratulate or envy someone who came out ahead.

phrases.en: I bought it during the sale and made a gain.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수지맞다'보다 덜 구어적이고 일반적으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more neutral, less colloquial way to say you profited.

explain_en: It is mostly used in casual forms like '수지맞았어요' or '수지맞는 장사' when you come out ahead. '이득을 보다' is similar, and '횡재하다' is for an unexpected big windfall.
